items.title: How to read papers effectively | Research reading technique
items.description:
=====
My name is Artem, I'm a neuroscience PhD student at Harvard University. 
🌎 Website and Social links: https://kirsanov.ai/
📥 "Receptive Field" neuro-newsletter: https://artemkirsanov.substack.com/
✨ Support me on Patreon to get access to Discord community: https://patreon.com/artemkirsanov
=====

In this video I talk about how to approach reading a research article, how papers are structured, in what order to read and how to highlight them.

🕒 OUTLINE:
00:00 Introduction
1:06 Wrong approach
items.why_watch: Harvard neuroscience PhD student Artem Kirsanov breaks down how academic papers are actually structured and why reading them front-to-back is usually the wrong approach. His method — understanding what each section is designed to do before deciding how deeply to engage with it — is immediately transferable whether you're a researcher or a curious non-specialist.

global_silver_linings.snippet: Hidden secrets of the narwhal’s twisted tusk have been revealed using the latest X-ray technology. Tusks of the species of whale native to the Arctic have long been the subject of myths—even being sold as ‘unicorn horns’ and believed to possess magical powers during the Middle Ages. Now, an international research team has solved the […] The post ‘Double Spiral’ Secret of Narwhal’s Twisted Tusk Revealed By High Tech X-Rays appeared first on Good News Network .
global_silver_linings.reason: Scientists have unlocked the hidden geometry inside one of nature's most mysterious structures, revealing that the narwhal's iconic tusk spirals in two directions at once — a reminder that the natural world still holds wonders we're only beginning to understand. Every discovery like this deepens our appreciation for the creatures we share the planet with.

news.title: Thomasina Miers’ recipes for spiced lamb-stuffed aubergine with aleppo chilli butter, and berry ripple ice-cream
news.snippet: A meaty, Middle Eastern style stuffed vegetable feast finished off with an ice-cold berry dessert There’s something delightfully retro about stuffed vegetables. They take me back to Delia Smith’s iconic Summer Collection cookbook , which blew my tiny mind when it came out in my early teens. Too sheltered to know about the e rage that had inspired Delia, I delved into my mother’s vegetable crisper with reverence, stuffing courgettes, tomatoes and aubergines with a zeal that had escaped me at school.
news.blurb: Thomasina Miers brings warmth and a touch of Middle Eastern magic to the gloriously retro stuffed vegetable, then sends it off with a berry ripple bow — a feast worth lingering over.

larder.seasonal_note: Zürich's weekly markets — Bürkliplatz on Tuesdays and Saturdays especially — are flush right now with the brief, glorious overlap of late Randen (Swiss beetroot) and the first Zwetschgen plums, those dark, jammy little things that beg to be roasted with a knob of butter and served over Quark for a slow morning breakfast.

fern_data.greeting: Did the ancient Greeks lie awake parsing their dreams the way we parse our anxieties — or did the dream feel, to them, more like a letter that had actually been delivered? Today's edition has that question, plus a narwhal's tusk hiding a double spiral no one expected, and a root cellar's worth of harvest wisdom for the obsessively prepared.
